20	Two root causes, both fixed:
21	1. Every page rendered its own `DesktopFrame > ScaledCanvas > DesktopShell` via
22	   `DesktopPageScaffold`, **and** `PageTransition` (`page-transition.tsx:22-24`)
23	   keys a `motion.div` on the location with `mode="wait"` — so every hop tore the
24	   chrome down and burned 220ms blank first. `ScaledCanvas` starts at `scale 0` /
25	   `visibility:hidden` until its layout effect runs, so each remount blanked the
26	   frame. Fix: `DesktopChrome` mounted once above the router, driven by the pure
27	   `desktopChromeForLocation()` map in `desktop-theme.ts`. Desktop app routes
28	   bypass `PageTransition`; mobile + public routes keep it unchanged.
29	2. Nav items had `padding: 0` and the active one `padding: 8px 22px` plus
30	   `font-weight: 700` under `justify-content: space-between`, so every label
31	   shifted on each page change. Fix: items always carry the active padding and
32	   reserve the bold width via a hidden `::after` sharing the grid cell; a
33	   separate `.tapt-desktop-nav-bubble` slides to the active item.
34	
35	Cascade primitives live in `desktop.css`: `@keyframes desktopBounceIn`,
36	`.dt-rise` (explicit `--dt-i` step / `--dt-d` offset) and `.dt-cascade`
37	(auto-indexes direct children 0..9). Delay = `--dt-i * 52ms + --dt-d`. A
38	reduced-motion block disables them and forces `opacity: 1` — required, because
39	they hide at `opacity: 0` and rely on the animation to reveal.
40	
41	**Measured**, both 1440×900 and 1194×834: chrome remounts **21/21 → 0/21**,
42	loader flashes **14/21 → 1/21**; wordmark/nav-label drift **0.00px** over 10 hops.
43	
44	Two acceptance probes (dev server on :5000, single instance —
45	[[dev-server-single-instance]], [[playwright-nix-chromium]]):
46	- `scripts/desktop-shots/probe-transitions.mjs` — chrome survival + loader flash.
47	- `scripts/desktop-shots/probe-topbar.mjs` — top-bar drift + bubble tracking.
48	
49	## Still owed
50	
51	- `npx jest` and `npm run build` were **not** run after the cascade landed (only
52	  `tsc`, which was green across all 19 edited files). Do these first.
53	- Visual side-by-side pass vs `docs/design/desktop-app/Taptpay Desktop.dc.html`.
54	- Mobile regression at 390×844 — must be byte-identical; the shell hoist must not
55	  disturb `PageTransition`'s Switch pinning ([[quickinv-pagetransition-fix]]).
56	- The one remaining probe "flash" is `/board-builder`'s own QR spinner
57	  (`board-builder.tsx:601`) inside the persisted frame — benign, not a regression.
58	
59	## Deliberate omissions the agents flagged (raise with Oliver, do not silently fix)
60	
61	- Drag sheets (`.ra-sheet`, `.pa-sheet`, `.ta-sheet`) are **excluded** from the
62	  cascade: they carry a live inline `transform: translateY(...)`, and a
63	  `both`-filled keyframe would pin them at `translateY(0)` and break the drag.
64	  Their contents cascade instead, so the sheet shell itself does not pop in.
65	- `.pa-dot` (chart peak marker) excluded — centred by `transform: translate(-50%,-50%)`.
66	- Rails are animated on `.rt-rail`/`.pt-rail`/`.tt-rail` themselves, never their
67	  slots: a transform on the slot makes it the containing block for the
68	  `position:absolute` rail and moves it.
69	- Property/trades analytics overviews sit inside `{!report && …}`, so returning
70	  from a generated report now replays the cascade. Accepted, easily gated.
71

73	
74	`trades-terminal.tsx` ~1221-1226: five empty CSS declarations (`color:;` ×4,
75	`background:;` ×1) in `.tt-quick-recipient > input`, `.tt-quick-channel button`
76	(+ `[aria-pressed="true"]`), `.tt-quick-success` (+ its button). Look like dropped
77	template interpolations; browsers discard them, so those quick-invoice controls
78	fall back to inherited colours.

8	two remaining external manual gates (real-device push and a staging Windcave flow).
9	
10	> **If you are picking this up cold and about to work on the terminal's "no
11	> payment board" option, read `docs/PLAN-2026-08-06-payment-links-no-board.md`
12	> first.** The corrected token flow and Phase 0 safety foundation are implemented
13	> and verified against an isolated PostgreSQL 16 database. Production rollout is
14	> still gated by the migration/deployment sequence and the external smoke checks

54	## 2. How to build a screen (the loop that has worked)
55	
56	1. **Read the design markup for that screen** in
57	   `docs/design/desktop-app/Taptpay Desktop.dc.html`. Screen offsets:
58	   retail 4a–4e at lines 40 / 233 / 302 / 526 / 766; property 2a–2e at
59	   1710 / 1947 / 2001 / 2217 / 2494; trades 3a–3e at 883 / 1076 / 1130 / 1354 / 1593.
60	   The rendered targets are `docs/design/desktop-app/screens/dt--*.png`.
61	2. **Read the prototype's logic** for that screen — the `<script type="text/x-dc">`
62	   block (~line 2621+). Property state atoms are unprefixed, trades are `tr*`,
63	   retail are `rt*`. That map is the interaction spec: what toggles, what animates,
64	   what a button does.
65	3. **Find the mobile page that owns the same logic** and reuse its endpoints,
66	   mutations and validation. Never invent an endpoint; never re-derive a fee or a
67	   GST rate that already exists in `lib/report-utils.ts`.
68	4. **Verify against the schema, not against the mobile page's variable names.**
69	   See §4 — three field-name assumptions have already been wrong.
70	5. Write the page as a single file with a page-scoped CSS template literal (class
71	   prefix per page: `rh-`, `rs-`, `rt-`, `ra-`, `ds-`, `ph-`). This matches the
72	   codebase's per-vertical-page convention.
73	6. **Verify** (§5), then commit that one screen with a message that states what was
74	   wired and what deviates from the design.

77	
78	- The canvas is exactly **1180×880**. `DesktopShell` renders a 66px header + 1px
79	  divider, then `.tapt-desktop-main` (1180×813, `position: relative`) holding your
80	  page. So a design coordinate `y` inside a screen maps to `y - 66` in your page.
81	- The design's own absolute offsets can be ported verbatim once you subtract that
82	  66 (and the body padding, if your container has any). 4c's rail and 4d's report
83	  blocks do exactly this and match the PNGs.
84	- Pass `showScope={false}` to `DesktopPageScaffold` when the screen draws its own
85	  scope control inside a column (every content page does).
86	
87	---

93	npx vite build                      # each desktop page must land in its own chunk

103	node scripts/desktop-shots/shot-property-home.mjs   # → /tmp/taptpay-desktop-2a/*.png
104	node scripts/desktop-shots/shot-trades-terminal.mjs # → /tmp/taptpay-desktop-3c/*.png
105	```

    feat(desktop): persistent chrome, sliding nav bubble, cascading entry
    
    Tablet/desktop navigation hard-cut between screens and flashed. Two causes:
    every page rendered its own DesktopFrame > ScaledCanvas > DesktopShell via
    DesktopPageScaffold, and PageTransition keys a motion.div on the location with
    mode="wait" — so each hop tore down the whole chrome and spent 220ms blank
    before the destination mounted. ScaledCanvas starts at scale 0 / visibility
    hidden until its layout effect measures, so every remount blanked the frame.
    
    - Mount the chrome once above the router (DesktopChrome), driven by a pure
      location -> {vertical, page} map. Desktop app routes bypass PageTransition;
      mobile and public routes keep it unchanged.
    - Scope the Suspense fallback to the page slot so a cold lazy chunk can no
      longer paint a full-screen loader over chrome already on screen.
    - DesktopPageScaffold defers to the hoisted chrome via context, and still draws
      its own when rendered standalone, so page tests keep working.
    - Nav items always carry the active padding and reserve the bold label width, so
      selecting a page cannot resize or shift them; a separate bubble slides to the
      active item.
    - Add desktopBounceIn + .dt-rise/.dt-cascade and sequence every screen's entry
      blocks, so the cascade is the transition. Interaction animations (modals,
      sheets, report renders, rail mode switches) are left alone.

    tablet 1194x834: chrome remounts 21/21 -> 0/21, loader flashes 14/21 -> 1/21.
